title: El Diario de Viaje
subtitle: Learn the past tense the easy way — fui, comí, visité — and tell your own travel stories in Spanish.

learningFocus.summary: This activity gives true beginners a gentle, game-based first look at the Spanish preterite (the simple past tense) in Pre-IG Stage 1 Spanish Unit 8. Students sort past-time words (ayer, anoche, el año pasado), then master "The Big 3" travel-story verbs — ir/ser (fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron), comer (comí, comiste, comió…) and visitar (visité, visitaste, visitó…) — by choosing the right form for each person while a 3D globe follows their journey. They tell apart fue meaning "went" from fue meaning "was" using context, match real travel photographs to Spanish sentences, build diary sentences from English prompts, and see that the same regular -AR/-ER patterns also work for Unit 7 verbs such as llevar and comprar, revising clothing vocabulary on the way. Students then rebuild a real chat about a trip and read a postcard, finishing with a 3D bonus runner in which they steer a train through the correct answer gates. Every level moves from recognising to producing the language, with instant feedback that names the exact part of the word to fix.

orient.objective: Use the past tense of ir/ser, comer and visitar (fui, comí, visité…) to say what you did on a trip.
orient.courseLink: This activity is Unit 8 (Holidays & Travel) in Pre-IG Stage 1 Spanish. It uses the clothing words from Unit 7 and gives you the past-tense tools you will need for travel stories and, later, IGCSE Spanish writing.
orient.mission: You are travelling the world and writing your travel diary — in Spanish! Seven easy levels take you from Madrid to Buenos Aires. Everything is in simple Spanish and every instruction is in English. Mistakes are fine: you always get a hint and a second try.
steps: Meet The Big 3 verbs below (tap the cards and see the endings).
Choose your best guess for the Hypothesis question.
Play the seven levels and watch your plane fly around the globe.
Check your Record, then write your Explain and Apply answers.
Finish the Knowledge Check and generate your Learning Evidence.
successCriteria: You will be able to tell a past-tense sentence from a present one using words like ayer and el año pasado.
You will be able to choose fui / comí / visité and the other forms for yo, tú, él/ella, nosotros and ellos.
You will be able to tell if fue means “went” or “was” from the rest of the sentence.
You will be able to write 3 short sentences about a trip in the past tense.
orient.realLife: Next time you meet a Spanish speaker, you can tell them “El año pasado fui a España y comí paella” — and they will understand you straight away.

predict.prompt: You want to say “Yesterday I ate tacos.” What do you think the Spanish is?
predict.hint: Yesterday is in the past, so the verb ending changes. It is fine to guess!

investigate.title: El Diario de Viaje
investigate.lede: Seven levels, one trip around the world. Pick the Spanish that fits — you get a second chance if you slip, plus a clear hint. Every level you finish sends your plane to a new city. Earn XP, keep a streak and climb the ranks.

record.intro: Every answer you gave is logged here automatically — your own practice record. Look for the words you got wrong first time.
record.emptyText: No answers yet. Play the levels in the interactive above.

explain.prompt: Look at your Record and choose ONE answer you got wrong or needed two tries for. Write the Spanish words from that task, explain the rule in English (for example: which ending goes with which person, or how you can tell fue means “went” or “was”), and write one correct new Spanish example of your own.
explain.lede: Quote a real task from your own Record — not a general rule from memory.
explain.skillFocus: Use your own practice record to explain a Spanish rule clearly, with a correct example.

apply.prompt: Imagine you went on a trip (real or imaginary). Write 3 short Spanish sentences: (1) say where you went using a form of ir and a past-time word (for example ayer or el año pasado); (2) say one thing you ate using a form of comer; (3) say one place or thing you visited using a form of visitar. Then add one line in English saying who the sentences are about (you, a friend, your family…).
apply.lede: Use the verb form that matches the person: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fueron — comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comieron — visité, visitaste, visitó, visitamos, visitaron.
apply.skillFocus: Use Unit 8 Spanish in a new, real-life situation with the correct verb form for the person.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which sentence is about the PAST?

options.label: El año pasado fui a México.

knowledgeCheck.explain: “El año pasado” means last year, so the verb is in the past: fui (I went).
“Nosotros” (we) always ends in -imos for -ER verbs in the past: comimos.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Match each English sentence to the correct Spanish.
knowledgeCheck.explain: Fui = I went; fue = it was (here from ser); visitaste = you visited; comimos = we ate.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Read: “Ayer fui a Madrid con mi familia. Visité un museo y comí paella. Fue muy divertido.” What did the writer eat?
